data.title: What Does Netcapital Inc.'s 28.62% Stock Drop Mean for Investors? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Outlines Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline
data.description:
What Does Netcapital Inc.'s 28.62% Stock Drop Mean for Investors? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Outlines Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline

What Does Netcapital Inc.'s 28.62% Stock Drop Mean for Investors? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Outlines Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline

PR Newswire

BENSALEM TOWNSHIP, Pa., Oct. 23, 2026

Suit alleges Netcapital Inc. failed to disclose key facts to investors from December 15, 2021 through September 3, 2026; lead plaintiff deadline is December 7, 2026

BENSALEM TOWNSHIP, Pa., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith today reported that a securities class action lawsuit is pending against Netcapital Inc. ("Netcapital" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: NCPL) on behalf of investors who acquired its securities from December 15, 2021 through September 3, 2026. The Netcapital Inc. case, Chance v. Netcapital Inc. et al., was filed on October 8, 2026 in the U.S. District Court District of Massachusetts (Case No. 1:26-cv-14584).

Investors with losses on Netcapital Inc. securities can contact the Law Offices of Howard G. Smith about the Netcapital Inc. lawsuit before the December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

Key deadlines and dates for Netcapital Inc. investors

  • Lead plaintiff deadline: December 7, 2026
  • Class period: December 15, 2021 through September 3, 2026
  • Complaint filed: October 8, 2026

What happened?

On August 10, 2026, the SEC filed a complaint against Netcapital and certain senior executives alleging, among other things, that Netcapital was involved in a fraudulent scheme to overstate the revenue of Netcapital. Specifically, from approximately October 2021 through January 2024, Netcapital improperly recorded nearly $14 million in revenue from sham consulting agreements which produced no real revenue for Netcapital. The recognition of this revenue inflated Netcapital's total revenue by approximately 345%. During this period, investors in Netcapital's public and private securities offerings invested over $25.6 million.

On this news, Netcapital stock fell $0.05 or 12.82%, to close at $0.35 on August 11, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

Then on August 17, 2026, the Netcapital disclosed that its independent registered public accounting firm, Fruci & Associates II, PLLC, had resigned.

On this news, Netcapital stock fell $0.09 or 28.62%, to close at $0.23 on August 18, 2026, thereby further injuring investors.

Finally on September 3, 2026, after market close, Netcapital disclosed that on Avi Liss had resigned as a member of the Board of Directors, and from all committees of the Board, including the Audit Committee, effective immediately. In his resignation letter, Liss stated that he was resigning "in light of the serious allegations recently asserted against the Company and certain current and former officers, directors, and other individuals" in the SEC Complaint.

On this news, Netcapital stock fell $0.05 per share, or 8.15%, to close at $0.58 per share on September 4, 2026. The following trading day, Netcapital stock fell a further $0.08 per share, or 13.15%, to close at $0.50 per share on September 8, 2026, thereby further injuring investors.

What is the Netcapital Inc. lawsuit about?

The Netcapital Inc. securities lawsuit alleges that, between December 15, 2021 and September 3, 2026, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Netcapital Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose that: (1) Over the Class Period, Netcapital improperly recognized material revenues from what were, in reality, sham consulting agreements with entities controlled by Defendant John Fanning; (2) The consulting agreements were backdated and in some cases forged, and Netcapital Advisors provided little if any meaningful consulting services; (3) The Portfolio Company transactions were improperly undisclosed related-party transactions involving John Fanning; (4) Netcapital's certifications pursuant to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 were false; and (5) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Netcapital Inc.'s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

"The lawsuit against Netcapital Inc. alleges that, among other things, the Company failed to tell investors that Over the Class Period, Netcapital improperly recognized material revenues from what were, in reality, sham consulting agreements with entities controlled by Defendant John Fanning. Netcapital Inc. investors who bought during the class period may be able to pursue their losses, and the December 7, 2026 deadline is where that process begins," said Howard G. Smith of The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith.

Next steps for Netcapital Inc. investors

Netcapital Inc. investors who suffered losses may contact The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith to learn about pursuing their claims.

Lead plaintiff motions in the Netcapital Inc. class action are due to the Court by December 7, 2026. For more information, visit the firm's website, email howardsmith@howardsmithlaw.com, or call (215) 638-4847.

If you purchased Netcapital Inc. securities during the class period, you may retain counsel of your choice, or you may take no action and remain an absent class member. No class has been certified in the Netcapital Inc. case so far.

Common questions from Netcapital Inc. investors

Who is eligible? Investors who acquired Netcapital Inc. securities from December 15, 2021 through September 3, 2026 and suffered losses may qualify for the class in the Netcapital Inc. shareholder lawsuit.

What is the deadline? Lead plaintiff motions in the Netcapital Inc. case are due by December 7, 2026.

Can I recover without being lead plaintiff? Yes, Netcapital Inc. investors may take no action and remain absent class members.

Does it cost anything? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith works on contingency, so investors pay no attorneys' fees unless there is a recovery, and any fees require court approval.

About The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith

The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith has helped injured investors recover their money for more than 15 years. The firm prosecutes securities fraud, takeover, and derivative litigation against public companies and their officers, directors, and advisors in federal and state courts nationwide, and has helped clients recover hundreds of millions of dollars in losses. Clients speak directly with a lawyer, who will promptly answer any question.

Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome.

data.title: Infinity Hires Meta Superintelligence Labs Chip Veteran and the CUDA Educator Who's Taught Two Million Engineers
data.description:
Infinity Hires Meta Superintelligence Labs Chip Veteran and the CUDA Educator Who's Taught Two Million Engineers

Aditya Om and Elliot Arledge join Infinity's race to make any AI chip inference-ready in days, not years, unlocking frontier AI on any chip

Infinity (Infinity Artificial Intelligence Institute), an automated AI research company building the software layer that makes any AI chip inference-ready, today announced two key hires to its engineering team. Aditya Om, a former senior software engineer at Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL), joins Infinity as Staff Inference Optimization Engineer, and Elliot Arledge, whose CUDA and LLM coding courses have taught skills to more than two million people, joins as Member of Technical Staff.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261023380240/en/

Infinity (Infinity Artificial Intelligence Institute) announces two key engineering hires: Aditya Om (left), a former senior software engineer at Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL), joins Infinity as Staff Inference Optimization Engineer, and Elliot Arledge (right), whose CUDA and LLM coding courses have taught skills to more than two million people, joins as Member of Technical Staff.

“We’re hiring engineers to solve the greatest engineering challenges of our generation,” said Jeremy Nixon, founder and CEO of Infinity. “Aditya built inference stacks inside Meta Superintelligence Labs’ silicon program. Elliot taught millions of engineers how kernels actually work. Now they’re building automated AI research systems that create stronger AI models and inference frameworks than humans have ever built, so that every chip can run frontier AI."

Om and Arledge join Infinity at a pivotal time, as the company scales Ignition, its autonomous AI agent that compresses years of chip software development into days. Ignition’s coding-agent controller autonomously bootstraps every layer of a chip’s software stack.

Before joining Infinity, Om led development of the software stack for MSL’s in-house training and inference chips, built the collective communications software stack for Lightmatter’s Passage and where he published Envise in Nature, and worked as an IoT systems design engineer at Intel. He holds a Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor.

“Joining the team was a no-brainer,” said Om. “Inference has taken the world by storm. We have a pivotal shift in front of us, touching all areas of our lives, similar to the internet in the mid-90s. Infinity's mission of automating research in inference optimization so that the software layer is shaped to the custom hardware is the groundbreaking work I am passionate about.”

Arledge is a self-taught kernel engineer and CUDA expert who, at 22, has built coding courses that have taught millions of people to train LLMs from scratch & optimize CUDA kernels. “Chips are the core bottleneck of our time, and that’s exactly why I wanted to join Jeremy and Infinity,” said Arledge. “It takes a stubborn team of highly skilled, highly coordinated, ambitious people to pull this off.”

Infinity is actively expanding its engineering team, seeking the best AI infrastructure and engineering talent to build the future of recursive self-improving AI systems. Contact careers@infinity.inc to learn more.

INFINITY.INC FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

What does Infinity do?
Infinity builds the software layer that makes any AI chip inference-ready. Its autonomous AI agent, Ignition, generates and optimizes inference software for new silicon in days, not years.

What is Ignition and how does it work?
Ignition is Infinity's AI research agent that autonomously writes, tests and optimizes the low-level compute kernels that determine how efficiently a chip runs AI models. It continuously improves through a real-world feedback loop, without human kernel engineers.

Why can't new AI chips compete with NVIDIA out of the box?
NVIDIA's CUDA ecosystem represents two decades of inference software development that rival chipmakers can't quickly replicate. Infinity closes that gap by automating the software development itself.

How fast can Infinity bring a new chip to production-ready AI inference?
In a published case study with d-Matrix, Infinity reached 92% of a new chip's theoretical peak performance within 10 hours of first hardware access, with three frontier models running end-to-end within 10 days.

Which chip companies is Infinity working with?
Infinity is currently in active partnership discussions with multiple major chip companies. Infinity's first live design partnership is with d-Matrix, whose Corsair chip runs production inference via the Infinity d-Matrix Cloud. Infinity also recently announced a collaboration with HP Inc. The two companies have been working together to use Infinity Autoresearch to optimize the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super model running on the HP ZGX Fury powered by NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip.

Who founded Infinity?
Jeremy Nixon founded Infinity. He is a former Google Brain researcher and co-founder of AGI House, a San Francisco AI community that has launched hundreds of startups.

Is Infinity hiring?
Yes. Infinity recently added Aditya Om (ex-Meta Superintelligence Labs) and Elliot Arledge (CUDA and LLM educator) to its engineering team. Infinity continues to hire Silicon Valley’s top research and inference-library engineers to build the future of recursive self-improvement (RSI). Openings are posted at infinity.inc/careers.

About Infinity

Infinity (Infinity Artificial Intelligence Institute) is an automated AI research company building the software layer that makes any AI chip inference-ready. Its AI research agent, Ignition, automatically generates, tests and optimizes the low-level compute kernels that determine how efficiently a chip runs AI models, compressing inference software development from years into days. Infinity's live design collaboration with d-Matrix powers the Infinity d-Matrix Cloud, and the company is currently in active partnership discussions with other major chip companies.

Founded in August 2025 and headquartered in San Francisco, Infinity is a privately held company backed by Touring Capital and prominent angel investors, including executives at major chip companies, researchers from OpenAI and Anthropic, and Infinity CEO and founder, Jeremy Nixon. Follow Infinity.Inc on X and LinkedIn and Jeremy Nixon on X and LinkedIn, or learn more at https://infinity.inc.

data.title: Hansa Biopharma announces positive Idefirix PAES results presented in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session at ASN Kidney Week
data.description:
Hansa Biopharma announces positive Idefirix PAES results presented in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session at ASN Kidney Week

Hansa Biopharma announces positive Idefirix PAES results presented in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session at ASN Kidney Week

PR Newswire

LUND, Sweden, October 23, 2026
  • The 1-year graft failure-free survival at 12 months post-transplant was 90%, which is clinically meaningful
  • Graft and patient survival were 92% and 98%, respectively  
  • Idefirix was generally well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with previous clinical trial experience

LUND, Sweden, October 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hansa Biopharma AB, "Hansa" (Nasdaq Stockholm: HNSA), today announced that data from the European Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES) study of Idefirix® (imlifidase) were presented during the High-Impact Clinical Trials oral session at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The abstract "FR-OR103 Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES): An Open-Label Post-Authorization Trial of 50 Imlifidase Crossmatch-Positive Deceased-Donor Kidney Transplants in Europe" was selected as a Late-Breaking Abstract at the congress.

Renée Aguiar-Lucander, CEO of Hansa Biopharma, said: "The presentation of the PAES study in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session highlights the scientific and clinical relevance of these findings and the potential of imlifidase to address a significant unmet need for highly sensitized patients awaiting kidney transplantation. We are encouraged by the continued interest from the transplant community in the growing body of evidence supporting imlifidase."

Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain and investigator for the trial said: "The successful completion of the PAES study provides important evidence in a patient population that continues to face significant challenges in accessing kidney transplantation. These findings add to the clinical evidence supporting the use of imlifidase to enable transplantation in highly sensitized patients with a positive crossmatch against a deceased donor."

ASN Kidney Week is one of the world's leading scientific meetings in nephrology and transplantation, bringing together researchers and clinicians to present the latest advances in kidney disease and transplantation medicine. The High-Impact Clinical Trials session features selected studies considered to represent some of the most clinically relevant and impactful research presented at the congress.

The abstract was presented by Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain, on behalf of the PAES study investigators.

Summary of the Abstract

Background

Imlifidase have a conditional approval in Europe since 2020. PAES (NCT05369975) is a controlled, non-randomized, open-label post-authorization efficacy and safety trial, designed to provide comprehensive data to support a full marketing authorisation of imlifidase (Idefirix®) in Europe.

Methods

Fifty highly sensitized (HS) patients who received crossmatch positive kidney offers received imlifidase treatment in line with the mode-of-action i.e. conversion of a positive crossmatch to a negative crossmatch and thereby enabling transplantation. All patients were unlikely to be transplanted under available kidney allocation systems, including prioritization programs for HS patients.

The primary trial objective was to assess graft failure-free survival at 1 year after transplantation. Secondary outcomes at 1 year includes kidney function assessed by eGFR, patient survival, graft survival, delayed graft function (DGF), antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) and safety.

Results

  • The graft failure-free survival was 90% at 1 year after transplantation in patients desensitized with imlifidase (n=50).
  • Graft and patient survival were 92% and 98%, respectively.
  • The mean eGFR calculated by MDRD was 51.04 mL/min/1.73 m2 (n=45).
  • DGF was seen in 40% of patients with a median duration of 14 days.
  • AMR occurred in 56% of recipients; however, no allograft loss was associated with AMR.
  • There were no new or additional safety signals found, and no imlifidase infusions were stopped due to infusion reactions.

Conclusion

Imlifidase enables kidney transplantation with a successful kidney function measured as eGFR at 1 year in patients desensitized. Imlifidase was well tolerated, with a safety profile consistent with prior experience and no unexpected or unacceptable risks observed.

Information about the trial is available at ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05369975

Notes to editors

About highly sensitized patients

Highly sensitized patients have pre-formed antibodies with a broad reactivity against human leukocyte antigens (HLAs). Those antibodies can cause damage to a transplanted organ and potentially graft loss.1 The presence of HLA antibodies means that highly sensitized patients have limited or no access to transplantation, as finding a compatible donor organ 

is particularly challenging.2,3 The immunological complexity of highly sensitized patients make them spend a longer time on transplant waiting lists, with an increased risk of dying while waiting for a suitable donor organ.4,5 Across the U.S. and Europe, highly sensitized patients comprise around 10-15% of all patients on transplant waiting lists.6,7

About Idefirix® (imlifidase)

Imlifidase is an antibody-cleaving enzyme originating from Streptococcus pyogenes that specifically cleaves and inactivates all immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody subclasses, including HLAs. It has a rapid onset and inactivates IgG-antibodies within hours after administration. The decrease in antibody levels creates a temporal antibody-free window of opportunity for highly sensitised patients to undergo transplant, thus enabling successful transplantation from an otherwise incompatible donor.

Imlifidase received a conditional marketing authorization valid throughout the European Union on 25 August 2020 and is marketed under the trade name Idefirix for the desensitization treatment of highly sensitized adult kidney transplant patients with a positive crossmatch against an available deceased donor. The use of Idefirix should be reserved for patients who are unlikely to be transplanted under the available kidney allocation system, including prioritization programs for highly sensitized patients.

The efficacy and safety of imlifidase as a pre-transplant treatment to reduce donor-specific IgG antibodies was studied in four phase 2 single-arm, studies in EU and US, a controlled Phase 3 study in US and in this European Post-Authorization Efficacy and Safety (PAES) study. 5,7,10-11 .

Full EU product information can be accessed via the initial Summary of Product Characteristics found here

Idefirix is exclusively out-licensed for transplantation in EU, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Iceland and Middle East and North Africa (MENA) to SERB Pharmaceuticals since July 1, 2026.

In the US, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted the Biologics License Application (BLA) for imlifidase in February of 2026 and assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) action date of December 19, 2026.

About kidney failure

Kidney disease can progress to kidney failure or End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), identified when a patient's kidney function is less than 15%.12 ESRD poses a significant health burden, affecting nearly 2.5 million patients worldwide.12 A kidney transplant is the treatment of choice for suitable patients with ESRD because it offers improved survival and quality of life benefits, and is cost savings compared to long-term dialysis. There are approximately 170,000 kidney patients in the U.S. and Europe waiting for a new kidney.13

About Hansa Biopharma

Hansa Biopharma AB is a pioneering commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing and commercializing novel immunomodulatory therapies to transform care for patients with acute or complex immune disorders. Hansa's proprietary IgG-cleaving enzyme technology platform addresses serious unmet medical needs in transplantation, gene therapy and autoimmune diseases. The company's portfolio includes imlifidase, a first-in-class immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody-cleaving enzyme therapy, which has been shown to enable kidney transplantation in highly sensitized patients, and HNSA-5487, a next-generation IgG-cleaving molecule that will be developed for Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS). Hansa Biopharma is based in Lund, Sweden, and has operations in Europe and the U.S. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm under the ticker HNSA. Find out more at  www.hansabiopharma.com  and follow us on LinkedIn.

PennyMac Financial Services, Inc. Reschedules Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call to 5:30 PM ET on Thursday, October 29

PennyMac Financial Services, Inc. (NYSE: PFSI) will announce results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, in a news release to be issued after the market close on Thursday, October 29, 2026. The conference call and live audio webcast is being rescheduled to 5:30 pm. Eastern Time from the originally scheduled 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

The release, webcast, and accompanying materials will be available online at pfsi.pennymac.com. A replay of the webcast will be available shortly after its conclusion.

Individuals who are unable to access the website but would like to receive a copy of the materials should contact our Investor Relations department at 818.264.4907.

About PennyMac Financial Services, Inc.

PennyMac Financial Services, Inc. (NYSE: PFSI) is a national financial services firm focused on the production and servicing of U.S. mortgage loans and the management of mortgage-related investments. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Westlake Village, California, it is one of the nation's largest mortgage producers and servicers, and one of the few lenders operating at scale across all three production channels. The company combines advanced technology with significant operational scale to serve home buyers, existing homeowners, and its institutional partners nationwide. Additional information about PennyMac Financial Services, Inc. is available at pfsi.pennymac.com.

data.title: Phase 3 RAINIER Results Supporting Best-in-Class Potential of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy Published in the New England Journal of Medicine and Presented at the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week 2026
data.description:
Phase 3 RAINIER Results Supporting Best-in-Class Potential of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy Published in the New England Journal of Medicine and Presented at the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week 2026

- Vertex is on track for the U.S. FDA Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) date of November 30 for potential accelerated approval of povetacicept –

- Data published in NEJM and presented at ASN highlight povetacicept’s unique trifecta of efficacy, favorable safety, and the simplicity of dosing at-home every 4 weeks with a low-volume autoinjector –

- Data presented at ASN include a qualitative study examining patient perspectives on current and emerging IgAN therapies, showing that 96% of participants preferred an autoinjector over a prefilled syringe, and 80% of participants preferred dosing every 4 weeks versus weekly dosing -

- New clinical studies of povetacicept underway including a study evaluating patient experience on povetacicept administered via autoinjector -

Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated (Nasdaq: VRTX) today announced the publication of Phase 3 RAINIER results for povetacicept in the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM), presentation of these data at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 in Denver, Colorado, and advancement of the povetacicept clinical research program in IgAN. Vertex will also host an investor event during ASN on October 23 at 6:15-7 p.m. MDT (8:15-9 p.m. EDT). Further details are below.

Data being presented include a pre-specified Week 36 interim analysis of the ongoing Phase 3 RAINIER trial of povetacicept, an engineered fusion protein and dual inhibitor of the BAFF (B cell activating factor) and APRIL (a proliferation inducing ligand) cytokines, in immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). RAINIER met its primary endpoint, with povetacicept achieving a 52.0% reduction from baseline in proteinuria at Week 36 and a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 49.8% reduction versus placebo (P<0.0001), while also meeting both secondary endpoints.

The Week 36 interim analysis of RAINIER demonstrated that the depth of proteinuria reduction from baseline was consistent across demographic, clinical and regional subgroups, including an unprecedented 54.2% reduction in urine protein to creatinine ratio (UPCR) versus placebo in North America. Additionally, findings showed that 42.2% of povetacicept-treated participants reached 24-hour UPCR <0.5 g/g, the threshold aligned with current Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guidelines, compared with only 6.2% on placebo. Importantly, these findings were observed on top of optimized supportive care in both treatment arms, including sodium-glucose co-transporter 2(SGLT2) inhibitor use in 65.8% of participants, which is among the highest reported of any contemporary IgAN trial.

“At just 36 weeks of treatment, povetacicept has delivered impressive efficacy results, together with favorable safety and convenient dosing at-home every 4 weeks in a low-volume auto-injector that can fit into the lives of IgAN patients, underscoring the potential of povetacicept to substantially impact and redefine expectations for disease control in IgAN,” said Carmen Bozic, M.D., Executive Vice President, Global Medicines Development and Medical Affairs, and Chief Medical Officer at Vertex. “We are grateful to the patients, investigators, and study teams who made RAINIER the largest and fastest-enrolling contemporary IgAN trial to date and look forward to the November 30th PDUFA target action date.”

“What stands out from the RAINIER results is the important clinical validation of simultaneously targeting BAFF and APRIL to address upstream drivers and kidney injury in IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept was specifically designed as a high-potency, high-affinity TACI fusion protein with broad tissue distribution to deliver this dual inhibition in order to target upstream pathogenic immune complex production,” said Richard Lafayette, M.D., Professor of Medicine (Nephrology) at Stanford University Medical Center and RAINIER Steering Committee Co-Chair, who presented the data at ASN Kidney Week. “The results observed with povetacicept are among the most compelling I have seen in IgAN and highlight the potential of povetacicept to become an important new treatment option for patients living with this chronic progressive disease.”

Vertex also presented findings from a qualitative study examining patient perspectives on the device design and administration of current and emerging IgAN therapies, “Patient Perceptions of Injectable Therapies Among Adults with IgAN: A Qualitative Study” (#TH-PO0473). The study included in-depth, one-on-one interviews with 25 U.S. adults living with IgAN. Participants were shown pictures and short videos of the devices and asked to assess key treatment administration-related attributes. Findings showed that 96% of participants (24 of 25) preferred the characteristics of an autoinjector over a prefilled syringe, citing features such as the needle not being visible and elimination of manual needle insertion. Additionally, 80% of patients (20 of 25) preferred dosing every 4 weeks versus weekly dosing, with the top reasons being convenience and travel or time away from home considerations.

Vertex also announced a new clinical trial underway for povetacicept:

  • PAVANT IgAN Patient Experience Study (NCT07890909), A Phase 3b, Open-label, Single-arm, Patient Experience Study of Povetacicept Injection (via Autoinjector) in Adults With Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy

Visit news.vrtx.com/kidney-congress for more information about Vertex’s presence at ASN Kidney Week 2026.

Investor Event

Vertex will host an investor event and webcast on October 23 at 6:15-7 p.m. MDT (8:15-9 p.m. EDT) in Denver, Colorado, to discuss the data for povetacicept in IgAN, the Company’s program in APOL1- mediated kidney disease (AMKD), and other highlights across its kidney disease portfolio.

A live webcast of the presentation and Q&A portions can be accessed through the Investor Relations section of Vertex's website at investors.vrtx.com. To ensure a timely connection, it is recommended that participants register at least 15 minutes prior to the scheduled webcast. An archived webcast will be available on the company's website in the “Investors” section.

About RAINIER

RAINIER (NCT06564142) is a global Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pivotal trial of povetacicept 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks versus placebo on top of standard of care in 605 adults with IgAN (N=557 in main cohort, N=48 in the exploratory cohort). The trial was designed to have a pre-planned interim analysis evaluating the percent change from baseline in UPCR for the povetacicept arm versus placebo after a pre-specified number of patients reach 36 weeks of treatment. Final analysis will occur at two years of treatment, with a primary endpoint of total estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope through Week 104. RAINIER is the largest trial conducted in IgAN and achieved full enrollment faster than any contemporary IgAN trial.

As previously reported, patients treated with povetacicept achieved a 52.0% reduction from baseline in 24-hour UPCR at Week 36, with a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction of 49.8% in 24-hour UPCR compared to placebo (P<0.0001).

The trial also met its secondary objective. For the first secondary endpoint, patients treated with povetacicept demonstrated a 77.4% reduction from baseline in serum galactose deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1) compared to an increase of +9.1% in the placebo group, yielding a reduction of 79.3% compared to placebo (P<0.0001). For the second secondary endpoint, in patients with baseline hematuria, 85.1% achieved hematuria resolution in the povetacicept treatment group compared to 23.4% in the placebo group, resulting in hematuria resolution of 61.7% compared to placebo (P<0.0001).

Povetacicept was generally safe and well tolerated. The majority of adverse events (AEs) were mild to moderate. The most common events (≥10% of participants in either treatment group) for the povetacicept group versus the placebo group were upper respiratory tract infection (18.3% vs 11.4%), nasopharyngitis (9.7% vs 12.4%), and injection site reactions (14.5% vs 2.2%). There were no serious adverse events (SAEs) related to povetacicept and no deaths in the trial. There were no opportunistic infections, and no discontinuations due to infections. As expected, anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) were observed; these ADAs had no impact on efficacy or the risk profile.

Results from the RAINIER trial support the Biologics License Application (BLA) for povetacicept, which has been accepted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for accelerated approval in adults with IgAN. The Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date is November 30, 2026.

The RAINIER trial continues in a blinded manner until the last patient enrolled completes 104 weeks. Patients in RAINIER who have completed the Week 104 visit are eligible to enroll in the open-label extension study (NCT07807995), “A Phase 3 Open-Label Study of Long-term Treatment With Povetacicept in Adults With Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy,” and receive an additional 104 weeks of treatment and follow-up.

About Povetacicept

Povetacicept is a dual inhibitor of the BAFF and APRIL cytokines, which promote B cell activation, differentiation and/or survival, and provides B cell control by inhibiting the ability of BAFF and APRIL to drive the pathogenesis of multiple immune-mediated diseases. Due to its engineered TACI domain, povetacicept has demonstrated improved binding affinity, potency, pharmacokinetics, and/or tissue distribution compared to other APRIL, BAFF, and dual BAFF+APRIL inhibitors in preclinical studies.

If povetacicept is approved by the FDA, Vertex plans to launch povetacicept as a low-volume (<0.5 mL) subcutaneous autoinjector delivered once every 4 weeks via at-home administration.

IgAN is the first of multiple indications that Vertex is exploring for povetacicept given its pipeline-in-a-product potential. There are ongoing studies including the Phase 2/3 OLYMPUS trial (NCT07204275) in primary membranous nephropathy (pMN) and the Phase 2 ETNA trial (NCT07501702) in generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG).

About IgA Nephropathy (IgAN)

IgAN is a serious, progressive, life-threatening kidney disease driven by uncontrolled autoreactive B cell activity and is the most common cause of primary glomerulonephritis, affecting approximately 330,000 people in the United States and Europe and more than 1.5 million globally. IgAN results from the deposition of circulating immune complexes, consisting of immunoglobulins and galactose-deficient immunoglobulin A (Gd-IgA1), in the renal glomerular mesangium, triggering kidney injury and fibrosis.

About Vertex

Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases and conditions. The company has approved therapies for cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia, acute pain and acromegaly, and it continues to advance clinical and research programs in these areas. Vertex also has a robust clinical pipeline of investigational therapies across a range of modalities in other serious diseases where it has deep insight into causal human biology, including IgA nephropathy, neuropathic pain, APOL1-mediated kidney disease, primary membranous nephropathy, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent Cushing's syndrome, autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, type 1 diabetes, generalized myasthenia gravis, and myotonic dystrophy type 1.

Vertex was founded in 1989 and has its global headquarters in Boston, with international headquarters in London. Additionally, the company has research and development sites and commercial offices in North America, Europe, Australia, Latin America and the Middle East. Vertex is consistently recognized as one of the industry's top places to work, including 17 consecutive years on Science magazine's Top Employers list and one of Fortune’s 100 Best Companies to Work For. For company updates and to learn more about Vertex’s history of innovation, visit www.vrtx.com or follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and X.

Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements as defined in the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended, including, without limitation, the statements made by Carmen Bozic, M.D., and Richard Lafayette, M.D., and statements regarding expectations for the potential accelerated approval of povetacicept in the U.S., expectations for new clinical trials planned for povetacicept, expectations for the RAINIER trial, expectations for the launch of povetacicept if approved by the FDA, expectations for the anticipated benefits of povetacicept, including its best-in-class potential, and the clinical status of and expectations for the Phase 2/3 OLYMPUS trial in pMN and the Phase 2 ETNA trial in gMG. Those risks and uncertainties include, among other things, that data from the company’s clinical programs may not support registration or further development in a timely manner, or at all, due to safety, efficacy, and other risks, that the potential accelerated approval and/or the anticipated commercial launch of povetacicept may be delayed, if it occurs at all, and other risks listed under the heading “Risk Factors” in Vertex's most recent annual report and subsequent quarterly reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission at www.sec.gov and available through the company's website at www.vrtx.com. data.title: What Does Anavex Life Sciences Corp.'s 6.35% Stock Drop Mean for Investors? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Outlines Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline
data.description:
What Does Anavex Life Sciences Corp.'s 6.35% Stock Drop Mean for Investors? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Outlines Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline

What Does Anavex Life Sciences Corp.'s 6.35% Stock Drop Mean for Investors? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Outlines Securities Fraud Class Action Lead Plaintiff Deadline

PR Newswire

BENSALEM TOWNSHIP, Pa., Oct. 23, 2026

Suit alleges Anavex Life Sciences Corp. failed to disclose key facts to investors from November 26, 2025 through August 28, 2026; lead plaintiff deadline is November 30, 2026

BENSALEM TOWNSHIP, Pa., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith today reported that a securities class action lawsuit is pending against Anavex Life Sciences Corp. ("Anavex" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: AVXL) on behalf of investors who acquired its securities from November 26, 2025 through August 28, 2026. The Anavex Life Sciences Corp. case, Kurey v. Anavex Life Sciences Corp. et al., was filed on September 29, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (Case No. 26-cv-08567).

Investors with losses on Anavex Life Sciences Corp. securities can contact the Law Offices of Howard G. Smith about the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. lawsuit before the November 30, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

Key deadlines and dates for Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors

  • Lead plaintiff deadline: November 30, 2026
  • Class period: November 26, 2025 through August 28, 2026
  • Complaint filed: September 29, 2026

What happened?

On May 11, 2026, the Company filed with the SEC a notification of late filing which disclosed it had "terminated the employment of Dr. Christopher Missling as the Chief Executive Officer of the Company on April 30, 2026 for, among other things, conduct that the Special Committee believed was inconsistent with Company Policy."

On this news, Anavex stock fell $0.18 per share, or 5.55%, to close at $3.06 on May 12, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

Then, on August 28, 2026, Anavex filed an Amended 2025 Annual Report with the SEC. The report stated, in part, that as a result of a review by the Special Committee, management, in consultation with the Audit Committee of the Board, "concluded that there was a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting that existed at September 30, 2025" and that "the Company's disclosure controls and procedures were not effective."

On this news, Anavex stock fell $0.19 per share, or 6.35%, to close at $2.80 on August 31, 2026, thereby injuring investors further.

What is the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. lawsuit about?

The Anavex Life Sciences Corp. securities lawsuit alleges that, between November 26, 2025 and August 28, 2026, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Anavex Life Sciences Corp.'s business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose that: (1) Anavex lacked adequate internal controls; (2) Anavex understated its potential regulatory challenges as a result of misconduct by former CEO Christopher Missling; and (3) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Anavex Life Sciences Corp.'s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

"The lawsuit against Anavex Life Sciences Corp. alleges that, among other things, the Company failed to tell investors that Anavex lacked adequate internal controls. Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors who bought during the class period may be able to pursue their losses, and the November 30, 2026 deadline is where that process begins," said Howard G. Smith of The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith.

Next steps for Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors

Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors who suffered losses may contact The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith to learn about pursuing their claims.

Lead plaintiff motions in the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. class action are due to the Court by November 30, 2026. For more information, visit the firm's website, email howardsmith@howardsmithlaw.com, or call (215) 638-4847.

If you purchased Anavex Life Sciences Corp. securities during the class period, you may retain counsel of your choice, or you may take no action and remain an absent class member. No class has been certified in the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. case so far.

Common questions from Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors

Who is eligible? Investors who acquired Anavex Life Sciences Corp. securities from November 26, 2025 through August 28, 2026 and suffered losses may qualify for the class in the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. shareholder lawsuit.

What is the deadline? Lead plaintiff motions in the Anavex Life Sciences Corp. case are due by November 30, 2026.

Can I recover without being lead plaintiff? Yes, Anavex Life Sciences Corp. investors may take no action and remain absent class members.

Does it cost anything? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith works on contingency, so investors pay no attorneys' fees unless there is a recovery, and any fees require court approval.

About The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith

The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith has helped injured investors recover their money for more than 15 years. The firm prosecutes securities fraud, takeover, and derivative litigation against public companies and their officers, directors, and advisors in federal and state courts nationwide, and has helped clients recover hundreds of millions of dollars in losses. Clients speak directly with a lawyer, who will promptly answer any question.
